One-step extension of a partial projective resolution
items.strategy: Let the current exact augmented complex end in a kernel object K. A chosen epimorphism from a projective object onto K supplies the next differential, and the image-equals-kernel statement is then built into the choice of K itself.

items.title: One-step extension of a partial injective resolution
items.strategy: Dualize the one-step projective extension: embed the current cokernel into an injective object, use that monomorphism as the next coaugmentation step, and read exactness off the chosen cokernel.

items.title: A chosen chain of projective covers gives a projective resolution
items.strategy: Iterate the one-step extension lemma on successive kernels. The statement names the choice boundary honestly: pointwise iteration for one object is allowed, while a global resolution functor is not produced here.

items.title: A chosen chain of injective embeddings gives an injective resolution
items.strategy: Iterate the dual one-step extension lemma on successive cokernels, again keeping the choice accounting explicit instead of collapsing it into a global functorial choice claim.

items.title: Under the Axiom of Choice, every module admits a projective resolution
items.strategy: Apply the general existence theorem to module categories using the published enough-projectives result rather than rebuilding the free-cover argument here.

items.title: Every module admits an injective resolution
items.strategy: Apply the general existence theorem to module categories and cite the published enough-injectives theorem with its existing choice boundary intact.

items.title: The iterated free-module resolution is canonical in ZF
items.strategy: Repeatedly take the free module on the underlying set of the current kernel. This gives a functorial exact free resolution without choosing bases or lifts; only the upgrade from free to projective uses the previously recorded choice boundary.

items.title: Augmentation-preserving maps of projective resolutions
Lifting a map through degree zero of a projective resolution
items.strategy: Use projectivity of the source degree-zero term against the target augmentation epimorphism to obtain the first square of a comparison map.

items.title: Extending a partial comparison map by one degree
items.strategy: The chain-map defect at stage n lands in the next cycle object because the previous squares already commute. Exactness makes that cycle a quotient of the next projective term, and projectivity lifts the defect.

items.title: Projective comparison maps exist
items.strategy: Start with the degree-zero lift and iterate the one-degree extension lemma. The proof is by an honest induction through the displayed resolutions, not by a later derived-category argument.

items.title: Extending a partial comparison homotopy by one degree
items.strategy: Given two partial comparison maps lifting the same object morphism, their difference at degree n is a cycle-valued defect after subtracting the already chosen homotopy correction. Projectivity of the source term lifts that defect into the next degree.

items.title: Projective comparison maps are unique up to chain homotopy
items.strategy: Apply the partial-homotopy extension lemma degree by degree to the difference of two lifts of the same morphism. The comparison map is not unique, but its homotopy class is.

items.title: Projective resolutions of the same object are homotopy equivalent over that object
items.strategy: Lift the identity on the resolved object in both directions and then use uniqueness up to homotopy on the two composites and the two identities.

items.title: Injective comparison maps exist
items.strategy: Pass to the opposite abelian category and dualize the projective comparison construction, keeping the morphism direction fixed when translated back to cochain language.

items.title: Injective comparison maps are unique up to cochain homotopy
items.strategy: Dualize the projective uniqueness theorem in the opposite category, then translate the resulting homotopy data back to cochain indexing.

items.title: Injective resolutions of the same object are homotopy equivalent under that object
items.strategy: Apply the injective comparison theorem to the identity in both directions and use uniqueness up to cochain homotopy on the resulting composites.

items.title: A projective or injective resolution is unique up to nonunique homotopy equivalence
items.strategy: Package the previous two homotopy-equivalence theorems while keeping the noncanonicity explicit: the equivalence class is forced, the chosen comparison map is not.

items.title: Comparison maps respect composition up to homotopy
items.strategy: A chosen lift of g∘f and the composite of chosen lifts of f and g are both comparison maps for the same underlying morphism, so uniqueness up to homotopy identifies them.

items.title: Comparison of the identity is homotopic to the identity
items.strategy: Apply the composition-up-to-homotopy proposition to id = id∘id and compare the chosen identity lift with the literal identity chain map.

items.title: The degree-zero horseshoe lift
items.strategy: Lift the right augmentation through the middle epimorphism, add it to the left augmentation, and use the finite coproduct theorem to keep the new degree-zero term projective.

items.title: The horseshoe kernel fits into a short exact sequence
items.strategy: Build the 3x3 diagram relating the two old kernels to the new kernel, then use the snake and nine lemmas to identify the resulting middle kernel sequence as short exact.

items.title: The inductive horseshoe step
items.strategy: Apply the degree-zero horseshoe construction to the short exact sequence of kernels from the previous lemma and iterate.

items.title: The horseshoe lemma for projective resolutions
items.strategy: Iterate the kernel step through every degree. The middle terms are finite coproducts of projectives, and the inductive kernel short exact sequences force exactness of the assembled augmented complex.

items.title: The horseshoe lemma for injective resolutions
items.strategy: Dualize the projective horseshoe theorem in the opposite category and translate back to cochain indexing, using finite products of injectives for the middle terms.

items.title: Horseshoe resolutions are compatible with morphisms of short exact sequences up to homotopy
items.strategy: Compare two horseshoe resolutions induced by a morphism of short exact sequences row by row and use comparison uniqueness to identify the resulting maps up to homotopy.

items.title: A split short exact sequence admits the direct-sum resolution
items.strategy: When the object sequence already splits, the obvious direct-sum complex is exactly the horseshoe construction with the chosen splitting maps built in from the start.

items.title: Schanuel's lemma in an abelian category
items.strategy: Take the pullback of the two projective presentations over the common target. The two projection maps from that pullback are epimorphisms with kernels the two original syzygies, and projectivity splits both sequences to produce the stable isomorphism.

items.title: Syzygies from two projective resolutions are stably isomorphic
items.strategy: Apply Schanuel to the first two surjections onto the object and then iterate that comparison along truncated resolutions when higher syzygies are involved.

items.title: The dual Schanuel lemma for injective copresentations
items.strategy: Pass Schanuel's lemma to the opposite abelian category and translate the result back from projective presentations to injective copresentations.

items.title: A projective object has a length-zero projective resolution
items.strategy: Place the projective object in degree zero with the identity augmentation. Exactness and the length-zero condition are immediate from the identity map.

items.title: Extension from subobjects of a generator detects injectivity
items.strategy: Use Zorn's lemma on the partially ordered set of extensions of a morphism A -> I across larger subobjects of B. The generator hypothesis reduces failure of maximality to a missing extension from some subobject of the fixed generator.

items.title: The one-step generator extension functor
The one-step generator map is a functorial monomorphism
items.strategy: The map M -> M(M) is a pushout of a coproduct of monomorphisms N -> U, so pushouts of monomorphisms keep it monic. Functoriality is inherited from functoriality of coproduct and pushout.

items.title: Transfinite iteration of the generator extension preserves monomorphisms and factorizes small-source maps
items.strategy: Successor stages inherit monomorphisms from the previous lemma. At limit ordinals, AB5 keeps the colimit maps monic, and a cofinality bound larger than the generator's size forces each map from a generator-subobject to factor through an earlier stage.

items.title: A sufficiently long generator-extension iteration is injective
items.strategy: At a limit ordinal whose cofinality exceeds the stated subobject bound, factor each generator-subobject map through an earlier stage, extend it at the next stage, and apply injectivity detection.

items.title: Grothendieck abelian categories have functorial injective embeddings
items.strategy: Follow the Stacks route visibly: define the one-step generator extension functor, prove its map is functorial and monic, iterate transfinitely using AB5 at limit stages and a cofinality bound on the generator, and finish with the generator-subobject injectivity test.

items.title: Every Grothendieck category has enough injectives, and every object admits an injective resolution
items.strategy: The theorem gives a functorial injective embedding for every object, hence enough injectives. Then iterate the general injective-resolution existence theorem on successive cokernels.

items.title: FALSE: enough projectives selects a projective resolution functor on all objects
items.strategy: Refute by separating pointwise existence from the stronger functorial projective-surjection datum.

items.title: FALSE: a comparison map between resolutions is unique as a chain map
items.strategy: Refute by the uniqueness-up-to-homotopy theorem, which leaves room for distinct lifts inside one homotopy class.

items.title: FALSE: two syzygies of an object are canonically isomorphic
items.strategy: Refute by Schanuel's stable-isomorphism conclusion and by an explicit stabilized resolution pair on the companion page.

items.title: FALSE: the degree-zero horseshoe lift is unique
items.strategy: Fix the standard split sequence of abelian groups and exhibit two distinct lifts of the identity right augmentation through its middle projection.

items.title: FALSE: every abelian category has enough projectives and enough injectives
items.strategy: Refute on two fronts: the Grothendieck theorem is one-sided toward injectives, and standard concrete abelian subcategories still fail enough projectives.

items.title: FALSE: every acyclic complex of projective objects is contractible
items.strategy: Refute with the standard periodic Z/4-complex with differential 2: it is acyclic and degreewise free over Z/4, but a contracting homotopy would force the identity to factor through 4 = 0.

items.title: A projective resolution of a cyclic abelian group
items.strategy: Write the two-term resolution 0 -> Z -> Z -> Z/n -> 0, verify exactness directly, and note that both terms are free abelian groups.

items.title: The canonical iterated free resolution of a module
items.strategy: Choose a small concrete module, take the free module on its underlying set, compute the first kernel explicitly, and iterate once more to show how the functorial ZF construction actually unfolds.

items.title: An injective resolution of an abelian group beginning with a divisible envelope
items.strategy: Embed a concrete abelian group in a divisible group, identify that group as injective over Z, and continue once on the cokernel to display the first two steps of an injective resolution.

items.title: Comparison maps between two resolutions of a cyclic group
items.strategy: Take two projective resolutions of the same cyclic group, choose an object map between their augmentations, and compute one degree-by-degree lift explicitly.

items.title: An explicit comparison homotopy
items.strategy: Construct two different comparison maps between the same small resolutions and write the homotopy that relates them term by term.

items.title: The horseshoe resolution of an extension of cyclic groups
items.strategy: Apply the horseshoe lemma to a short exact sequence of cyclic or nearly cyclic abelian groups and compute the first differentials in the direct-sum middle resolution.

items.title: Schanuel's lemma for two presentations of a module
items.strategy: Choose two short projective presentations of the same module, form the pullback comparison object concretely, and read off the resulting stable isomorphism.

items.title: Two projective resolutions with nonisomorphic first syzygies
items.strategy: Start from the basic resolution of Z/n and stabilize it by adjoining a free summand to both degree-zero and degree-one terms. The two kernels are then Z and Z⊕Z, which are stably but not literally isomorphic.

items.title: A category with enough injectives but not enough projectives
items.strategy: Work in the abelian category of torsion abelian groups. Enough injectives come from torsion divisible hulls, while a nonzero projective would lift a nonzero map to Z/p across all quotients Z/p^n -> Z/p, forcing an element of unbounded p-power order in a torsion group.
